info.title: CLARA API
info.summary: Clinical Logbook for Automated Research Assistance — REDCap API replacement
info.description:
Two surfaces (REQ-API-001): the REDCap-compatible data API at `POST /api/` (and `GET /api/`) with the caller token as the `token` parameter in the request body or query string (never an `Authorization` header, REQ-API-010), and the administration API under `/api/v1/`. The administration surface is reachable only from the trusted internal path (REQ-TECH-018): every request carries a valid `X-Internal-Service-Token` and — except for the pre-authentication endpoints of §4.3 — the authoritative `X-Internal-User-Id` of the acting user. The browser MUST NOT call `/api/v1/*` directly (GD-1).

Conventions (`Design/API_Endpoints_Design.md` §1): UTC and UTF-8; system timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` in UTC; absent optionals are `null`. Administration errors share the shape `{ "error": <stable code>, "message": <human-readable>, "status": <http status> }`; data-API errors are rendered in the requested response format (`json`: `{ "error": "…" }`, `csv`: a single line).

This document is hand-maintained (REQ-TECH-004, REQ-API-002) and served at `GET /openapi.json`; the interactive UI is the vendored Swagger UI bundle at `GET /docs`.

servers.description: The Go API process. nginx routes only POST /api/ (plus the PHP application) publicly; /api/v1/* and the documentation endpoints stay off the public network (Technology_Stack_Design.md §5).

get.description: Unauthenticated; reports liveness without returning data. `503` with `status: degraded` when the bounded database check fails.
The hand-maintained specification covering both surfaces, served from the API binary.
Interactive documentation from the vendored `swagger-ui-dist` bundle pointed at `/openapi.json`. Internal-only routing per Technology_Stack_Design.md §5.

post.description:
One endpoint dispatched by the `content` parameter with an `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` body. With `content=record`, a call carrying `data` is an import, one without it an export; deletion needs `action=delete`. Unknown parameters are accepted and ignored, never rejected (REQ-API-017). The token is the `token` parameter — never read from an `Authorization` header (REQ-API-010). Survey-link tokens are accepted only for the calls that render and fill their (record, instrument) pair: `content=metadata` (that instrument only) and a record import scoped to that record and instrument; everything else is 403 `Permission denied` (§3.10, REQ-API-083).

Error bodies are rendered in the requested response format (§3.2): 401 `Invalid token`, 400 `Invalid content`, 403 `Permission denied`, 403 `Project in analysis mode` for writes to an analysis-mode project, 429 `Rate limit exceeded` (with `Retry-After`).

parameters.name: Accept
parameters.description: text/csv is the REDCap default rendering; application/json selects JSON.

200.description: The result of the requested `content`. The JSON shape depends on `content` — see the examples. Record imports answer per-row result rows (or `{"count": N}` with `returnContent=count`, REQ-API-142); validation failures are per-record, not request-level (REQ-API-034).

schema.description: Result rows; `generateNextRecordName` answers a single object and `returnContent=count` answers `{"count": N}`.

importResultRows.summary: content=record import — result rows (REQ-API-034; import_record_id 1 added, 2 updated, 0 validation error)

value.import_form_name: Validation error: age: TYPE_INVALID — value "abc" is not a valid integer; status: CHOICE_INVALID — value "9" is not a choice of "status"

schema.description: The same result as CSV — the REDCap default when neither `format` nor `returnFormat` says otherwise. Streamed, quoted per standard CSV rules, honoring `csvDelimiter` (REQ-API-029).

get.summary: REDCap-compatible data API via query string (REQ-API-009)
get.description: `GET /api/` with the same parameters in the query string MUST also work. Behaviour, responses and errors are identical to `POST /api/`.

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Project API token or survey-link token (§3.10).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Only `delete` dispatches; `export`/`import` are accepted and never override the `data` rule (REQ-API-012).

parameters.name: returnFormat
parameters.description: Takes precedence over `format` for the response encoding (REQ-API-013).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: `flat` is normative — one row per (record, event); `wide` is the simplified compatibility mode (§3.6.2, DEV-API-1).

parameters.name: records
parameters.description: Repeated values or the REDCap indexed syntax `records[0]=…` (REQ-API-015).

parameters.name: filterLogic
parameters.description: Branching-logic expression filtering which records are returned; never changes the sensitivity level (REQ-API-025, §3.6.3).

post.description:
Called by the PHP application after successful OAuth2/LDAP authentication, or with `source: "local"` and the password for table-based login (GD-18). Exempt from `X-Internal-User-Id` (DEV-API-16); it still requires the service token. The API reports success and audit-logs it but MUST NOT create or store a session (GD-1).

Processing order: local credential check (or an unexpired `first_factor` handle standing in for the hash check where a second factor guards the account, REQ-API-131) → account-active rule (`account_expired` / `account_disabled`) → two-factor gate (`mfa_required`, `bad_mfa_code`, `tfa_enrollment_required`) → bootstrap-admin promotion → `auth_source`/`last_login_at` update → audit `login_success`.

handle_mfa.summary: Second call of a two-factor challenge with the handle from verify-password (REQ-API-131)

race.summary: Finalizing call of a failed named-source credential race (DEV-API-5 detail)

401.description: `account_not_found` — no user row for the email (REQ-AUTH-006); `bad_password` — no stored hash or mismatch (the two are not distinguished, GD-18); `mfa_required` `{"error":"mfa_required","method":"totp|email"}`; `bad_mfa_code`; `tfa_enrollment_required` `{"error":"tfa_enrollment_required","user_id":<id>}` under `AUTH_REQUIRE_2FA`; `first_factor_expired` (REQ-API-131). All audit `login_failure` where applicable.

403.description: `account_disabled` (including auto-disable by the inactivity rule) or `account_expired` (`valid_until` passed) — REQ-AUTH-052/053.

post.summary: Side-effect-free password verify for the named-source credential race (§4.3, REQ-API-123, DEV-API-17)
post.description: Runs the login endpoint's hash check and account-active rule only — no `last_login_at`/`auth_source` write, no audit event, no user object; login finalizes exactly once through `/api/v1/auth/login`. Pre-authentication: service token only. For an account a second factor still guards, the `ok` answer carries the `first_factor` handle (5 minutes, bound to one user id) that the challenge's second login call presents in place of the password (REQ-API-131).

200.description: `status` ∈ `ok | bad_password | account_disabled | account_expired`. `first_factor` and `expires_in` appear only on `ok` for an account a second factor still guards.

post.description: Records the `logout` audit event. Destruction of the PHP session remains the PHP layer's responsibility, performed after this call (GD-1).

post.summary: Request a password-reset link (Sequence H, REQ-API-119)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only (DEV-API-16). Always 202 with an identical body — whether or not a matching active local account exists (no enumeration, REQ-AUTH-062). When one does, emails the set-password link with a single-use `reset` token. Rate-limited per address and IP (default 3/15 min/address). Audit `password_reset_requested` (address + IP, never the token).

202.description: Accepted — identical body regardless of account existence.

post.summary: Set the new password with a reset token (REQ-API-120)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only. Constant-time hash verification, purpose `reset`, expiry, single use; success stores the bcrypt hash, consumes the token, invalidates all outstanding tokens of the account and audits `password_reset_completed`. No temporary password exists (REQ-AUTH-062). Any failure — unknown, expired, consumed or wrong-purpose token — answers the generic 401 `invalid_setup_token` (causes are not distinguished).

post.summary: Accept an invitation — set the invited user's own password (REQ-API-121)
post.description: Pre-authentication: service token only. As `/api/v1/auth/password-reset/complete` for purpose `invite`; audits `invite_accepted`; generic 401 `invalid_setup_token` on any failure. Login afterwards runs the full second-factor gate (REQ-AUTH-060).

get.description: Requires `is_admin`; a call by a non-admin is rejected (403 `forbidden`).

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. A new account → 201; a disabled account with the same email is re-enabled → 200 (re-enabling resets the inactivity clock, REQ-AUTH-053). The optional password is stored only as a bcrypt hash (REQ-AUTH-050), never returned or logged. Audit `user_created` (`re_enabled` flag, `valid_until`).

200.description: A disabled account with this email was re-enabled.

put.description: Requires `is_admin`; idempotent (REQ-API-042). Any change that would leave zero enabled administrators (an `is_admin` revocation, a disabling, or both in one call) is rejected 409 `conflict` with nothing written and no audit entry (REQ-API-136). `valid_days` re-sets `valid_until` (`0` → indefinite); `password` set/resets the local hash and an empty string clears it. Disabling a user denies the effective permissions of that user's API tokens at call time (REQ-AUTH-033). Audit `user_updated` with the changed attributes.

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Sends the invitation email with a single-use `invite` token to the account's address; a re-invite replaces any outstanding invite token (the old link dies). The token value is never in the response. 409 `smtp_not_configured` without a relay (the admin then sets the password directly). Audit `user_invited`.

put.description: Self-service. The current password is verified against `password_hash` first (failure → 401 `bad_password`, audit-logged, counted toward the REQ-AUTH-035 lockout), then the new bcrypt hash is stored. Accounts without a local credential → 409 `no_local_credential`. Sessions are not revoked (DEV-AUTH-13). Audit `password_changed`.

401.description: `bad_password` — the current password did not verify.

409.description: `no_local_credential` — the account has no local password.

get.description: Self-service; also valid in the pending-first-factor context under a mandate. Never returns the secret or a code.

200.description: The current method and enrollment time.

post.description: Returns the shared secret and its `otpauth://` URI — shown once; pending until confirmed.
A valid current RFC 6238 code activates `totp` and returns the recovery codes exactly once; a wrong code → 400 `bad_code`. Audit `tfa_enrolled`.

200.description: `totp` is active; recovery codes are returned once.

post.description: Sends a confirmation code to the account address via the SMTP relay; rate-limited per account.
Activates `email`, returns the recovery codes once. Audit `tfa_enrolled`.

200.description: `email` is active; recovery codes are returned once.

post.description: Requires a valid current code or recovery code; sets the method to `off` and clears secret/codes. Audit `tfa_disabled`.

Requires `is_admin`. Deletes the account's `user_two_factor` row back to `off` (lost device/email). No endpoint ever returns a secret, pending code, or recovery code outside its single enrollment/activation response. Audit `tfa_reset`.

get.description: Project visibility only (`is_admin` or member, REQ-AUTH-026); projects outside the acting user's visibility do not appear (REQ-API-007).

200.description: Dashboard summaries of every visible project.

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Creation is single-arm (REQ-DB-011, DEV-API-4): the API creates arm 1 only, together with its first event `baseline` (`unique_event_name = baseline_arm_1`, timepoint `period = 0`) and one instrument `instrument`. The removed attributes (`end_provision`, the `option_*` flags, `agreed_to_end_user_contract`, `event_names`) are rejected as unknown attributes (400 `invalid_request`). A duplicate `project_name` → 409. Audit `project_created`.

201.description: The created project (`id` + the supplied fields + `creation_time`).

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only` + project visibility. Full metadata plus structure plus the acting user's effective permissions — the same result the boundary applies to every call, surfaced so the PHP layer can gate rendering with the control absent from the DOM. Nothing is ever absent from `permissions.arms[]`/`grants[]`; the caller never infers a level from a missing entry (REQ-AUTH-069). This read authorizes nothing; every endpoint re-checks at call time (REQ-AUTH-033).

put.description: `project_admin` (an `is_admin` user is covered by REQ-AUTH-023). Body: any subset of the creation metadata fields — omitted fields are unchanged (idempotent, REQ-API-042). A duplicate `project_name` → 409. Metadata changes are audit-logged with old and new values (`project_updated`).

200.description: The updated project object (same shape as GET, `permissions` included).

get.description: Requires `is_admin`. `role` is `null` for a role-less member (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022); `token_present` reports existence without revealing the value (REQ-API-005).

put.summary: Add, change role, rotate token or remove a member (REQ-API-054/055)
put.description: Requires `is_admin`. The single mutation point for membership, keyed on the body: `{"role": "data-entry"}` adds (201, with the new token returned once); `{"role": null}` makes the member role-less; `{"rotate_token": true}` rotates — the previous token is invalid immediately; `{"remove": true}` removes the member and invalidates the token. Audit `membership_changed` plus `token_issued`/`token_rotated`/`token_revoked`. The token value never appears in logs or audit details.

200.description: Role change (member object), rotation (member object with the new token) or removal (`{"ok": true}`).

201.description: The member was added — the member object with the new token, returned once for display (REQ-API-055).

get.description: Self-service: `{uid}` MUST equal the acting user and the acting user MUST be a member; any other case is a uniform 403 `forbidden` (never disclosed as missing, REQ-API-007). The value MUST NOT be logged. No audit event for the fetch itself — it is credential plumbing.

Requires `is_admin`. Roles are project-scoped (REQ-AUTH-024) and not limited to preset examples (REQ-AUTH-020). `arms` always carries an entry for every arm; `grants` lists only the (instrument, event) pairs whose grant differs from their arm default (REQ-AUTH-069).

post.description: Requires `is_admin`. Body is the role object minus `id`; an arm absent from `arms` defaults to `no_access` / `export_none` (REQ-AUTH-019 — no implicit access). A duplicate name within the project → 409. Audit `role_created`.

put.description: Requires `is_admin`. Body is the same shape as POST, replacing name, `project_admin`, arm defaults and grants in one transaction; a pair omitted from `grants` reverts to its arm default, and an `arms` map missing an arm sets that arm to `no_access` / `export_none`. Unknown `{rid}` → 404; duplicate name → 409; an unmapped `event`/`instrument` pair → 400 naming it, nothing applied. Members holding the role pick the change up on their next request without re-authentication (REQ-AUTH-033). Audit `role_updated` with the before/after permission set.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`. Events are in the canonical per-arm order (GD-15); `period` is `null` when the event has no timepoint.

200.description: The project's arms, each carrying its events.

post.description: `project_admin`. `arm_num` is the next 1-based number (a duplicate → 409 `conflict`). Audit `arm_created`.

delete.summary: Delete an arm — or reset the last one (REQ-API-060, REQ-API-128)
delete.description: `project_admin`; the path follows the master plan verbatim (ASM-API-1). An arm that still has events or data → 409 `conflict` (DEV-API-6) — unless it is the project's last remaining arm: that one cannot go either, and the call instead renames it to `arm_1`, keeping its id, `arm_num` and events. The answer is then 200 with the renamed arm object. Audit `arm_deleted`, or `arm_updated` with `last_arm_reset` on the rename.

200.description: The last remaining arm was renamed to `arm_1`.

put.description: `project_admin`; idempotent. The full list of the project's arm ids; a partial or foreign list → 400. Writes `position` only — every arm keeps its id and `arm_num`, `unique_event_name` values and stored data are untouched. Audit `arm_reordered`.

order.description: The full ordered list of the project's arm ids.

get.summary: List all events of all arms (REQ-API-061)
get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`. Canonical per-arm order (GD-15): events with a `period` ascending by period (ties by position), then events with `period = null` ascending by position.

200.description: All events in canonical per-arm order.

post.description: `project_admin`. The API derives `unique_event_name = <label>_arm_<n>` (REQ-DB-011); a duplicate label within the same arm → 409; the new event takes `position` = end of the arm's list. `period` optional — `null`/absent = no timepoint (GD-15). Audit `event_created`.

put.description: `project_admin` (path verbatim, ASM-API-1); idempotent. Any subset of `{event_name, period, safe_region_start, safe_region_end}` — `period: null` clears the timepoint (the event becomes user-orderable, GD-15). A label change re-derives `unique_event_name`; a collision → 409. An event that already holds data keeps its values — the rename updates the stored `unique_event_name` key in the same transaction (ASM-API-4). Audit `event_updated` with old and new values.

delete.summary: Delete an event — or reset the last one (REQ-API-063, REQ-API-133)
delete.description: `project_admin`. Removes the event together with its instrument–event mapping pairs; values keyed on the event's `unique_event_name` become unreachable, so the change is breaking in analysis mode (§4.21). A project always keeps at least one event: deleting the last remaining event instead resets it to the plain baseline state — renamed to `baseline`, `period` reset to 0, safe region cleared — answering 200 with the renamed event object. Audit `event_deleted`, or `event_updated` with `last_event_reset`.

200.description: The last remaining event was reset to the baseline state.

put.description: `project_admin`; idempotent. The full ordered list of the supplied arm's event ids (a partial list → 400). Writes `position` (1…n); the canonical order of GD-15 then governs the display. Audit `event_reordered` with the new order.

order.description: The full ordered list of the arm's event ids.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`.

200.description: The project's instruments in position order.

post.description: `project_admin`. The name is unique within the project (REQ-DB-013; a duplicate → 409). `position` = end of list. Audit `instrument_created`.

put.description: `project_admin`; idempotent. The full ordered list of the project's instrument ids (a partial list → 400). The GD-8 record-identifier invariant MUST hold after reordering — a violation → 400 `invalid_request`. Audit `instrument_reordered`.

`project_admin`; idempotent. Any subset of `{name, is_survey, branching_logic}`. A rename keeps the name unique — a collision → 409, an empty or non-string name → 400 `validation_error`. The rename is a label: stored values are keyed by field name and event, so nothing is rewritten. An invalid branching expression is rejected at design time → 400 `validation_error` (REQ-VAL-029). Audit `instrument_updated` with old and new values.

400.description: `validation_error` — ill-formed expression (REQ-VAL-029) or an empty/non-string name; `invalid_request` for other malformed bodies.

delete.summary: Delete an instrument — or reset the last one (REQ-API-066, REQ-API-127)
delete.description: `project_admin`. Removes the instrument together with its fields, their stored values (same transaction) and its mapping pairs; losing recorded values makes the change breaking in analysis mode (§4.21). An expression that survives the change naming a doomed field → 409 `conflict`. A project always keeps at least one instrument: deleting the last remaining one only deletes its fields and renames the shell to `instrument` — id, position, survey flag and branching logic stay — answering 200 with the object. Audit `instrument_deleted` with the removed field and value counts, or `instrument_updated` with `last_instrument_reset`.

200.description: The last remaining instrument was reset — fields deleted, shell renamed to `instrument`.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`. The instrument's fields in position order, with all data-dictionary attributes (REQ-DB-013).

post.description: `project_admin`. Body is the field object minus `id`/`position` (appended at the end of the list). The field name is lower-case alphanumeric + underscore, unique within the project (duplicate → 409); names longer than 26 characters are accepted. `validation_type` must be empty, a built-in structured type, or an existing `validation_types` name (anything else → 400 `validation_error`, REQ-VAL-010/042); `direct_identifier` defaults to `1` for `email`, `MRN`, `international phone` or `national phone` (REQ-EXP-020). `calculation` is only allowed with `field_type = calculated`; expressions are validated at design time (REQ-VAL-029/033/034). Audit `field_created`.

400.description: `validation_error` — expression, validation type or name problem; `invalid_request` for a malformed body.

post.summary: Create fields in one all-or-nothing batch (REQ-API-132)
post.description: `project_admin`. A non-empty array of field objects exactly as accepted by the single-field POST; unknown attributes anywhere, an empty or missing array, or an entry without `field_name`/`field_type` → 400. All entries are validated against one shared dictionary view — a name used twice inside the batch collides on its second occurrence (→ 409), and a calculated entry may reference an earlier entry of the same call. Any rejected entry creates nothing. `acknowledge_breaking` (analysis mode) is read from the top level of the body. Audit `field_created` per field, in the same transaction.

201.description: The created field objects, in request order.

put.description: `project_admin`; idempotent. The full ordered list of the instrument's field ids (a partial list → 400). The GD-8 record-identifier invariant MUST hold after reordering — a violation → 400 `invalid_request`. Audit `field_reordered`.

`project_admin`; idempotent. Any subset of the attributes — including a `field_name` rename (stored values renamed in the same transaction, REQ-VAL-014), the `calculation` expression, the `branching_logic` expression, and the `direct_identifier` flag. A change to a calculated field's expression triggers recomputation of all project records in the same transaction (REQ-VAL-037). Audit `field_updated` with old and new values.

400.description: `validation_error` — expression, validation type or name problem; `invalid_request` for a malformed body.

delete.description: `project_admin`. The field's stored values are removed in the same transaction (DEV-API-5); a field referenced by an active expression → 409 `conflict` (§4.2). Audit `field_deleted` with the count of removed values.

204.description: The field and its stored values were removed.

get.description: Any authenticated user; read-only. The four built-in structured types plus every `validation_types` row. The pattern is included for advisory client-side hints only — server-side validation remains authoritative (REQ-VAL-002). Registry entries are added by inserting a database row; there is no write endpoint in phase 1.

post.summary: Test a calculation expression against a record (REQ-API-096)
post.description: `project_admin` + record visibility under the data-access-group rule (REQ-AUTH-045). Optionally supplies a draft `expression`; omitted = the field's stored expression. The call MUST NOT store or modify anything — it is the designer's test action. Each evaluation problem carries an explicit flag (REQ-VAL-038): `missing_value | non_numeric_operand | division_by_zero`.

expression.description: Draft expression; omitted = the field's stored expression.

200.description: The evaluation result with explicit problem flags.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`. Each array lists the events an instrument is mapped to; an empty array = mapped to no event.

put.description: `project_admin`; idempotent. The full matrix for the supplied arm, replacing that arm's mapping (an unknown instrument or event name → 400). Unmapping never deletes anything: the pair's `data` and `instrument_completion` rows stay in place and become visible again when the pair is mapped back — non-breaking in every mode (§4.21). Audit `mapping_updated`.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only` + record visibility (REQ-AUTH-045). All visible records, with their instruments per event in the instrument order of each arm and a three-state completion state per (record, event, instrument): only `finished` is stored; `no_data`/`some_data` are computed per row. A survey-marked instrument always reports `finished` (GD-9). The response MUST NOT contain field values; a record-status read is not a record view.

put.description: Data access ≥ `view_edit` on the record's arm (+ record visibility); idempotent. A workflow annotation, not data entry — writes no field value and is not subject to analysis-mode write rules. Unknown record/event/instrument → 404; an unmapped pair → 409; a survey-marked instrument → 409 (its `finished` state is automatic). Audit `instrument_completed` / `instrument_uncompleted`.

state.description: `finished` sets the marker; `unfinished` clears it back to the derived no_data/some_data.

get.description: The response is streamed (REQ-TECH-011). Record selection follows the data-access-group rule; sensitivity follows the acting user's export level for the (instrument, event) pair of each exported column (the REQ-API-026 ladder) — an `export_none` pair contributes no columns and a request with no permitted pair in scope is 403. Columns belonging to no pair follow the most protective level among the pairs in scope. Known parameters validate strictly; unknown parameter names stay accepted and ignored (REQ-API-017). Every call is audit-logged as an `export` event with `surface: "ui"`, the project, and the sensitivity level; a rejected call writes no audit entry.

parameters.name: arm
parameters.description: Repeatable (`arm=1&arm=3`) — restricts the export to those arms (REQ-EXP-003). An arm the caller cannot export → 403; an unknown arm number → 404.

parameters.name: csvDelimiter
parameters.description: Single character; empty value = comma (REQ-EXP-013). CSV only.

get.description: `is_admin` only; any other acting user gets the uniform 403 (ASM-API-2, finding F2). Reverse chronological. Entries MAY carry the `token` column and payload values — the trail is the sole sanctioned carrier (REQ-AUD-007). The endpoint is read-only: no endpoint exists that writes, updates, or deletes audit data (REQ-DB-024).

200.description: One page of audit entries, newest first.

get.summary: Per-field history of one record (REQ-API-079…081, REQ-API-137)
get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only` on the record's arm + project visibility + record visibility. Chronological by default (`order=chrono`), transparent across the yearly rollover; `order=newest` serves the same entries reverse-chronologically with the cursor paging backwards (DEV-API-23) — the read direction the data entry form uses to derive current values. For `create`, `old` is `null`; for `delete`, `new` is `null` and the `old` values are the deleted values (REQ-AUD-009). Read-only with respect to the audit trail.

get.summary: Issue / read the survey link of a pair (REQ-API-082, GD-9)
get.description: Data access ≥ `view_edit` on that pair (REQ-AUTH-069) + record visibility. The instrument MUST be survey-marked and mapped to the event — otherwise 400. The link is stable per (project, record, instrument, event) until revoked; an instrument mapped to three events has three distinct links. `collected_at` is `null` until the first response is saved through the link and never changes afterwards. Audit `survey_link_issued`.

delete.summary: Revoke the survey link of a pair (REQ-API-082)
delete.description: Revokes the link token of that pair; links of the same instrument at other events stay valid. The revocation takes effect immediately (REQ-AUTH-040). Audit `survey_link_revoked`.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only`.

post.description: `project_admin` (an `is_admin` user is covered, REQ-AUTH-023). The name is unique within the project (REQ-AUTH-043; a duplicate → 409). Audit `dag_created`.

delete.description: `project_admin`. Removes the group and its member assignments; while records are still assigned → 409 `conflict` (ASM-AUTH-4; a rejected call writes no audit entry). Audit `dag_deleted`.

put.description: `is_admin` (REQ-AUTH-044). Exactly one active group when `groups` is non-empty (otherwise 400); an empty list clears. Audit `dag_membership_changed`.

Self-service for the acting member (who holds a non-empty assignment). The group MUST be one of the member's assigned groups (otherwise 400). The switch takes effect immediately (REQ-AUTH-046). Audit `dag_active_switched`.

put.summary: Assign a record to a group (REQ-API-091)
put.description: `project_admin` (REQ-AUTH-048); the record MUST be visible to the acting user (REQ-AUTH-045). `{"group_id": null}` unassigns. Group scope and export transformation are orthogonal (REQ-API-092). Audit `dag_record_assigned`.

get.description: Any authenticated user.

Any authenticated user. The render-time read for the PHP shell: a flat key→text map overlaid on the English strings the application carries (English is the source of truth and lives in the PHP layer — REQ-DB-031); a key absent from the map renders in English. Without `language`, the acting user's stored UI language is served (default `en`). An unknown or disabled language → 400.

parameters.name: language
parameters.description: Language code; omitted = the acting user's stored UI language.

get.summary: Translation keys with the current translation (REQ-API-099)
get.description: `is_admin`. A missing key falls back to English (REQ-DB-031).

200.description: The keys with text and missing flag.

put.description: `is_admin`. An empty `text` removes the translation (fallback to English, REQ-DB-031). Audit `i18n_updated` per changed key.
Any authenticated user acting on themselves. The language MUST be enabled (otherwise 400); the default is `en`. The setting persists across sessions (REQ-DB-008).

Any authenticated user acting on themselves. The value MUST name an installed theme (`bootstrap` | `darkly` | `yeti`, REQ-TECH-027), or `null` to clear the personal override and follow the installation default `UI_THEME` (REQ-CFG-031); an unknown identifier → 400. The API stores the value and never serves CSS.

post.description: `is_admin`. One-shot — a second execution for the same project → 409 (the idempotency state is the `project_ended` audit event). Atomic: the audit row and the data change are written by the same-transaction writer. `delete` removes the project's stored record data (EAV rows, `record_entities`, `survey_links`, `anon_offsets`) keeping metadata, structure, roles/memberships/tokens and the audit trail; `anonymize` applies the `export_de_identified` pipeline in place — irreversible.

get.description: Data access ≥ `read_only` + project visibility.

200.description: The mode and whether a staging set is open.

put.description: `is_admin` alone — the project's own `project_admin` gets a 403 (GD-20, 2026-09-27); idempotent. Allowed transitions: development→production (`keep_data` required — `false` deletes the record data with the end-provision `delete` scope), production→development, production→analysis, analysis→production, analysis→development. Any other pair (including development→analysis) → 409. No mode change while a staging set is open — every transition is rejected until the set is committed or discarded. Audit `project_mode_changed` with old/new mode and the `keep_data` decision.

200.description: The new mode (`records_deleted` set only for the delete-on-transition case).

post.description: `project_admin`; production mode only (409 otherwise); a second set while one is open → 409. Snapshots the live design — structure endpoints then read and write the staged design for `project_admin` users while every data-facing endpoint keeps serving the active design until commit. Audit `staging_started`.

get.summary: Staging state plus the staged diff (REQ-API-106)
get.description: `project_admin`. The diff is computed against the active design and classifies each change breaking / non-breaking per the normative table of §4.21.

changes.reason: deleting a field makes its stored values inaccessible

post.description: `project_admin`. If the staged diff contains breaking changes and `acknowledge_breaking` is not `true` → 409 listing them. On success the snapshot is applied to the live structure tables in one transaction (the whole set activates at once, GD-20) and the staging row is removed. A commit does not recompute calculated values (owner decision 2026-09-29). Audit `staging_committed`.

409.description: The diff contains breaking changes and `acknowledge_breaking` was not supplied — the response lists them.

post.description: `project_admin`. The staging row is removed without applying. Audit `staging_discarded`.

get.description: `is_admin`. The effective values: the stored row when present, the seeded default otherwise. The rate limiter reads them per request, so an applied change takes effect on the next request without a restart.

put.description: `is_admin`; any subset of the fields (idempotent). Validation: `rate_limit_enabled` a boolean; `rate_limit_rpm` an integer ≥ 1; `rate_limit_block_minutes` an integer 1–1440 — else 400; unknown attributes → 400. Audit `settings_updated` with the old and new value of each changed key; a PUT that changes nothing writes no entry.

200.description: The full settings object after the update.

InternalServiceToken.name: X-Internal-Service-Token
InternalServiceToken.description: The shared service secret (REQ-AUTH-011/012): compared in constant time, never logged, enforced regardless of any other configuration (REQ-CFG-023). Missing or invalid → 401 `service_token_invalid` + audit `admin_rejected`. Configured per System_Configuration_Design.md §3.3.

InternalUserId.name: X-Internal-User-Id
InternalUserId.description: The acting user's id — authoritative for authorization (REQ-AUTH-013): the API applies that user's effective levels; the PHP layer adds none. Unknown or disabled user → 403 + audit `admin_rejected`. Set by the trusted PHP layer only; the proxy strips it from every externally-originated request.

UserIdPath.name: uid
UserIdPath.description: User id of the project member.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque cursor encoding the last-seen (created_at, id); from the previous page's `next_cursor`.

BadRequest.description: `invalid_request` — malformed JSON body or a missing/invalid attribute (§4.2).

AdminForbidden.description: `forbidden` — insufficient permission, or a project/record outside the acting user's visibility (uniform, never disclosed as missing — REQ-API-007); unknown/disabled acting user (audit `admin_rejected`).

NotFound.description: `not_found` — an unknown path resource (user, project, arm, event, instrument, field, or group).

Conflict.description: `conflict` — a state violation (§4.2): duplicate name, deletion that would strand data or leave zero enabled administrators, an expression-referenced delete, a mode transition outside the allowed set, staging conflicts, unacknowledged breaking changes.

RateLimited.description: 429 — the per-source-IP budget is exceeded; `Retry-After` names the remaining whole seconds of the blockout (REQ-API-038/113, §3.9).

Retry-After.description: Remaining whole seconds of the blockout, rounded up.

DataApiInvalidToken.description: Missing/invalid token — the same body whether or not the token exists (REQ-AUTH-032).

DataApiForbidden.description: `Permission denied` — insufficient permission (incl. export_none, read-only import); `Project in analysis mode` for writes to an analysis-mode project (GD-20, REQ-API-109).

Retry-After.description: Remaining whole seconds of the blockout, rounded up.

AdminError.description: The administration error shape (§4.2): `error` is a stable machine code callers may branch on; `message` is human-readable and never leaks internal details (REQ-API-006).

error.description: Stable machine code: invalid_request, validation_error, service_token_invalid, account_not_found, bad_password, invalid_setup_token, forbidden, account_disabled, account_expired, not_found, conflict, internal.

status.description: The HTTP status, mirrored in the body.

DataApiError.description: The data-API error body in JSON rendering (§3.2); with `returnFormat` csv (the default) the same text is a single CSV line.

DataApiRequest.description: The common data-API parameters (§3.1), `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`. Unknown parameters are accepted and ignored, never rejected (REQ-API-017). Indexed array syntax (`records[0]=…`) and repeated single values are both accepted (REQ-API-015).

token.description: UUID project API token or survey-link token (§3.10). Body or query; never read from an Authorization header (REQ-API-010, REQ-AUTH-031).

action.description: With `content=record` only. `export`/`import` are accepted and never override the `data` rule; `delete` is the only action that dispatches; any other value → REDCap-style error (REQ-API-012, DEV-API-24).

returnFormat.description: A present returnFormat takes precedence for the response encoding (REQ-API-013).

type.description: `flat` is normative — one row per (record, event); `wide` is the simplified compatibility mode of §3.6.2 (DEV-API-1).

filterLogic.description: Branching-logic expression (§3.6.3, Data_Validation_Design.md §7) filtering which records are returned; export only (REQ-API-025); never changes the sensitivity level.

rawOrLabel.description: Choice fields as codes or labels (REQ-API-027).

data.description: Import rows in either REDCap encoding (§3.7.1): the indexed form parameters `data[i][key]=…`, or a single `data` parameter holding a JSON array of record objects (DEV-API-24). Its presence makes the call an import (REQ-API-012, REQ-API-031). Indexed parameters win when both encodings are present.

returnContent.description: With a record import: `count` answers `{"count": N}` for the rows applied; anything else keeps the §3.7.2 result rows (REQ-API-142).

tz.description: IANA timezone name or ±HH:MM offset — timezone of collection for the call's date/date-time values; default APP_TIMEZONE (import only, GD-16, REQ-VAL-041).

overwriteBehavior.description: Accepted and ignored (REQ-API-017): import always upserts.

ContentValue.description: The dispatcher of the data API (REQ-API-012). With `content=record`: a call carrying `data` is an import, one without it an export; deletion needs `action=delete`.

User.description: The user object (§4.3), returned by login and every user endpoint.

auth_source.description: The source the account last authenticated through (REQ-AUTH-005).

ui_theme.description: `null` when the account follows the installation default theme UI_THEME (GD-26).

last_login_at.description: `null` when the account has never logged in.

provider.description: The identity provider (or LDAP source id) the PHP layer authenticated against.

password.description: Local login only; never logged (REQ-AUTH-036). Ignored on a race-finalizing call (REQ-API-135).

mfa_code.description: The second factor for the two-factor gate (GD-21).

first_factor.description: The handle from verify-password standing in for `password` on the second call of a two-factor challenge (REQ-API-131, DEV-API-19).

source_name.description: The authentication-source name the user selected; recorded in login audit details, never affects identity resolution or authorization (REQ-AUTH-067).

attempts.description: Per-source outcomes of a failed named-source credential race (source-id → outcome, e.g. bad_password, unreachable); MUST never contain credentials (REQ-AUTH-036). Such a call reports a failure and authenticates nothing (REQ-API-135).

first_factor.description: Only on `ok` for an account a second factor still guards: stateless handle bound to one user id, signed with a key derived from INTERNAL_SERVICE_TOKEN (REQ-API-131).

password.description: Optional — stored only as a bcrypt hash (REQ-AUTH-050), never returned or logged.

UpdateUserRequest.description: Any subset; idempotent (REQ-API-042). Any change leaving zero enabled administrators → 409 (REQ-AUTH-068, REQ-API-136).

password.description: Set/reset the local hash; an empty string clears it (REQ-AUTH-036).

secret.description: Base32 shared secret — shown once, pending until confirmed (REQ-AUTH-056).

code.description: A current RFC 6238 code, an emailed confirmation code, or a recovery code (disable).

role.description: `null` for a role-less member (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022).

MemberWithToken.description: The token value appears only in the add/rotation response — never in logs (REQ-API-005) and never in audit details.

MemberMutation.description: The single mutation point for membership (REQ-API-054): add (`role`), change role (`role`, `null` = role-less), rotate the token (`rotate_token`), remove (`remove`).

role.description: Role name; null or omitted = role-less (full permissions, REQ-AUTH-022).

arms.description: Per-arm default; keys are arm numbers as strings; every arm of the project appears (REQ-AUTH-019).

grants.description: Only the (instrument, event) pairs whose grant differs from their arm default (REQ-AUTH-069).

delete_values.description: The delete-instrument-values right — a boolean, never a level (REQ-AUTH-070).

RoleInput.description: The role object minus `id` (POST and PUT — REQ-API-143). An arm absent from `arms` defaults to no_access / export_none.

ProjectCreate.description: The creation fields of the simplified `projects` (GD-17, REQ-DB-006). The removed attributes (`end_provision`, `option_*`, `agreed_to_end_user_contract`, `event_names`) are rejected as unknown attributes (400, REQ-API-052).

ProjectUpdate.description: Any subset of the creation metadata fields — omitted fields are unchanged (idempotent, REQ-API-042).

ProjectDetail.description: Full metadata plus structure plus the acting user's effective permissions (REQ-API-126).

EffectivePermissions.description: The effective evaluation of Authentication_Authorization_Design.md §4.1 for the acting user — one `arms[]` entry per arm carrying that arm's default, one `grants[]` entry per mapped (instrument, event) pair as it resolves for that caller; nothing is ever absent from either list (REQ-AUTH-069).

period.description: Timepoint — days after baseline; `null` = no timepoint (GD-15).

EventUpdate.description: Any subset; `period: null` clears the timepoint (GD-15). A label change re-derives unique_event_name — a collision → 409.

field_name.description: Lower-case alphanumeric + underscore, unique within the project.

field_type.description: text, notes, dropdown, radio, checkbox, matrix, calculated, date fields, …

validation_type.description: Empty, a built-in structured type, or a validation_types registry name (REQ-VAL-010/042).

direct_identifier.description: Defaults to true for email, MRN, international phone, national phone (REQ-EXP-020).

FieldInput.description: The field object minus `id`/`position` (appended at the end of the list).

FieldUpdate.description: Any subset of the attributes — including a field_name rename (stored values renamed in the same transaction, REQ-VAL-014), the calculation expression (triggers recomputation, REQ-VAL-037), the branching logic and the direct_identifier flag.

acknowledge_breaking.description: Analysis mode only (REQ-API-111): re-send after a 409 naming the breaking change.
Read from the top level of the body (analysis mode, REQ-API-111).

regex.description: Advisory client-side hint only — server-side validation remains authoritative (REQ-VAL-002).

mapping.description: instrument name → the unique_event_names it is mapped to; an empty array = mapped to no event.

details.description: Entries MAY carry the token column and payload values — the trail is the sole sanctioned carrier (REQ-AUD-007).

new.description: `null` for delete — the `old` values are the deleted values (REQ-AUD-009).

url.description: The stable public link carrying the link token — stable per (project, record, instrument, event) until revoked.

collected_at.description: `null` until the first response is saved through the link, then never changes (REQ-DB-041, REQ-AUTH-071).

strings.description: Flat key→text map; a missing key renders in English (REQ-DB-031).

breaking.description: Classification per the normative table of §4.21.

rate_limit_rpm.description: Requests per rolling minute per source IP (default 600).

rate_limit_block_minutes.description: Blockout after exceeding the budget (default 10; REQ-API-113).
